Lessons for the corporate world from the world's biggest festival - the Indian
Parliamentary Elections 2019.🎉🎊 The verdict is almost clear, everyone across
the world has sensed the one-sided victory of a man and a party which won by
the right marketing mix. Wondering how? 🤔 Here are my takeaways from the
hashtag#indianelections2019 1\. It is very important to have a good leader. A
good leader gives confidence to the entire team under him or her. 🗣 2\. It is
all about team-work. A leader cannot win alone. Having the right team brings
greater laurels to the entire organisation. Individual victories may not help
you win a cricket match🏏. Similarly, you need to take along the team together
and help each other. 🤝 3\. Nothing can defeat your plan if you have the right
strategy.🎖 4\. Choosing the right pain-points and addressing them helps you
win the trust of the people.🤗 5\. Victory and defeat is part and parcel of the
game. But what should not be ignored are analysis and contemplation.🔎 Being in
the corporate world, what are the learnings for you? Please share them in the
comments. PS: No political comments and abusing please. Pure learning or
takeaways only will be entertained. hashtag#leadership hashtag#linkedin

post_content:
Unless you always wanted to become a car engineer, don't waste your time on
self-driving car online courses and especially specializations. Self-driving
car technology is only needed for a handful of companies in the world. Most of
them will not develop it themselves: they will buy the best one available on
the market. To choose such specialization is like to decide to learn
everything about the internal combustion engine or lithium-ion batteries. I'm
sure, it's very entertaining, but don't expect much as an employment
potential.

profile_headline: Working on Youth Empowerment Initiatives in India and Oman
post_content:
I believe if you're in India, you must definitely have someone in your family
or friends or professional network who studied Mechanical Engineering, Civil
Engineering, Electrical Engineering and then hired by companies like Infosys,
Wipro, TCS etc. These companies hire a Non-IT candidate, train them for months
and put them to code or test or maintain softwares together with CS-IT
candidates. This is the greatest example of 'Unity in Diversity'😅 I don't have
any objection with this but what sense it makes to study a different branch of
engineering if the engineers aren't making innovation in respective fields.
Also, it makes me bring the conclusion that long 4 years of studies is of no
use if only months of training is good enough to start working. I may sound
you rude sometime but these are the areas we really need to think upon.
